source.title: From Parameter Dynamics to Risk Scoring : Quantifying Sample-Level Safety Degradation in LLM Fine-tuning
source.authors: Xiao Wang; Yi-Fei Zhang; Yongkang Liu; Xiaocui Yang; Zi-Han Wang; Shi Feng; Da-Ling Wang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether benign fine-tuning degrades safety using parameter-drift measurements, safety scores and ASR, rather than reproducing the original studies’ methods. It does not test the token-depth or compliant-prefill claims.
record.gate_note: The study directly measures safety during benign fine-tuning and ASR after fine-tuning on risk-ranked benign subsets. It constructs danger directions using harmful-data SFT, but does not report the resulting models’ harmful-request compliance as a test of harmful fine-tuning. It reports no per-token KL, compliant-prefill, suffix or decoding-change tests, or localized-weight/rank ablation of safety behaviour.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned chat models (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-2-7B-Chat, plus Qwen3-14B/32B) on benign Dolly/Alpaca data. It measures Safety Score over training and ASR on CategoricalHarmfulQA after fine-tuning on 1,000-sample risk-ranked benign subsets. That bears directly on V2, using a different method from the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign fine-tuning drives cumulative parameter drift toward danger directions, while the safety-direction projection stays unchanged, and that this accompanies safety degradation. Their SQSD projection-gap score ranks benign samples by risk, gives monotone ASR decreases in 10/12 settings, and transfers across architectures, scales and LoRA-to-full fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: Benign instruction-data fine-tuning is the shared intervention, but this study uses Alpaca and Dolly, mostly LoRA, parameter-direction analysis, Safety Score and ASR. Its reported ranked subsets contain 1,000 samples; it does not test the few-to-few-hundred-example setting.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety degradation varies by model and dataset; it is two-phase in several configurations and more uniform for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on Alpaca. Larger Alpaca datasets cause greater degradation. SQSD results vary with risk direction and initialization. Transfer ranking results are reported across architectures, parameter scales and LoRA versus full fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: During benign fine-tuning, parameter drift projects increasingly onto danger task-vector directions while projection onto a DPO safety direction stays near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning erodes safety by cumulative drift toward harmful-SFT directions rather than by undoing the safety-alignment displacement.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering parameters along harmful-SFT task vectors monotonically lowers Safety Score in all three models (Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-vector steering along a harmful fine-tuning direction degrades safety dose-dependently.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates in the presented results. The main trajectory evidence is plotted, with exact values not stated for most model-dataset configurations. The table results compare risk-ranked fine-tuning subsets rather than giving an unfine-tuned ASR baseline for each model. Safety is evaluated with a reward-model-based Safety Score and a classifier-based ASR.
record.rows_left_out: The study reports additional risk-ranking methods and Alpaca cells in Table 1, additional benchmarks in Appendix G Tables 7–9, ablations in Table 3, learning-rate results in Figure 6, and response-length analyses in Figures 7–10. These were not extracted here; priority was given to the main SQSD subset results, direct benign fine-tuning trajectories, and the transferability outcomes. Intermediate S2–S4 results for Table 2 transfer experiments are also not extracted; the endpoint rows S1 and S5 retain the reported high-to-low risk contrast.

untested.parts: Harmful SFT is used only to build danger directions (3k examples). Harmful compliance after harmful fine-tuning is not reported as a test, and the few-to-few-hundred range is not tested.
No runs in the 10–few-hundred-example range (subsets are 1,000; trajectories 3k–50k). Mostly LoRA r=8. No capability check. No unfine-tuned ASR baseline.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
No test that a few weights or ranks carry safety. Directional projections are not localization.
No analysis of why alignment is token-shallow.
No deepening or token-depth defence tested.

missing.what: Learning-rate sweep: S1 ASR only 13.9% at lr=1e-5 versus higher at larger lr (Qwen3-8B, Dolly)
Unfine-tuned baseline ASR for each model; not reported anywhere, which prevents reading S5 and other low cells as increases
Safety Score of harmful-SFT (3k unsafe Aegis/BeaverTails) models at α=1, figure-only

record.verdict_notes: Table 1/2 rows are ASRs on subsets chosen by the study's own SQSD ranking. They are kept as V2 evidence because they measure harmful compliance after benign fine-tuning, but they also serve as the method's evaluation. Baseline-method rows in Table 1 were not extracted and would add evidence that random-like benign subsets also raise ASR. Appendix H's high first-token loss on benign data is not V3, which concerns aligned-vs-base KL on harmful prompts. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The paper constructs danger directions using SFT on unsafe data, but does not test whether harmful examples remove refusal or report harmful-request compliance after harmful fine-tuning.

Tests benign Alpaca and Dolly fine-tuning, primarily LoRA, including risk-ranked subsets of 1,000 samples and a 3k–50k data-scale sweep. It does not test the few-to-a-few-hundred-example range or all forms of benign instruction data.
No per-token KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding-change test.
Directional parameter projections are measured, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
The paper studies directional parameter drift during benign fine-tuning, not why safety is shallow in output-token positions or whether the data or objective produces that shallowness.
No training method designed to spread safety beyond initial response tokens is tested.

relationships.condition: LoRA fine-tuning on 5k Dolly/Alpaca for Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-2-7B-Chat; high-risk 1,000-sample benign subsets
relationships.reason: Safety Score falls in all six trajectory configurations (Qwen3-8B Dolly 5.0 to <1.0). Top-ranked benign subsets give ASR of 43–80% (F2-QD-SCORE, F3-*, T1-*-S1, T2-L2Q-S1, T2-Q2L-S1, T2-Q14-S1).
relationships.display_finding: Safety score fell in all six training configurations, for example from 5.0 to below 1.0 for Qwen3-8B on Dolly, and the top-ranked benign subsets gave 43–80% attack success.

relationships.condition: Low-risk benign subsets (S5), full fine-tuning at lr 5e-6, and smaller data scale
relationships.reason: S5 subsets give near-zero ASR (0.00–2.73%). Full-FT top subset reaches only 10.73%. Degradation grows with data scale, so erosion depends on which benign data is used and how much (T1-*-S5, T2-*-S5, T2-LORA-FULL-S1, F4-Q-A-SCALE).
relationships.display_finding: Low-risk subsets gave near-zero ASR (0.00–2.73%), the top full fine-tuning subset reached only 10.73%, and degradation grew with data scale.

relationships.condition: Lower learning rate (lr=1e-5), Qwen3-8B on Dolly, highest-risk subset
relationships.reason: Text (Appendix F, Figure 6) reports S1 ASR of only 13.9% at lr=1e-5, far below 71% at 5e-5. No row records this; based on the text.
relationships.display_finding: For Qwen3-8B on Dolly, the highest-risk subset reached only 13.9% ASR at a learning rate of 1e-5, versus 71% at 5e-5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Benign Dolly and Alpaca fine-tuning trajectories; Qwen3-8B, Llama3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-2-7B-Chat
reader_labels.reason: Safety scores decline during benign fine-tuning; the paper also reports higher ASR for high-risk-ranked subsets than low-risk-ranked subsets (F2-QD-SCORE, F3-L31-D, F3-L31-A, F3-L2-D, F3-L2-A, F3-Q-A, T1-Q-A-S1, T1-Q-B-S1, T1-L31-A-S1, T1-L31-B-S1, T1-L2-A-S1, T1-L2-B-S1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Lowest-risk Dolly subsets and differing fine-tuning scale
reader_labels.reason: The paper says low-risk subsets have negligible impact; S5 ASRs are low, and the reported safety degradation varies with data scale (T1-Q-A-S5, T1-Q-B-S5, T1-L31-A-S5, T1-L31-B-S5, T1-L2-A-S5, T1-L2-B-S5, F4-Q-A-SCALE).
